correctness.rationale: Direct exponentiation of the two invariant Hamiltonian blocks gives the two X-state concurrence candidates. Their dependence on \(\nu(D)=\sqrt{g^2+D^2}\) is monotone, so each has at most one crossing. Solving the two equality conditions gives the stated piecewise \(D_-\) and \(D_+\). Independent evaluation on the source benchmark across several temperatures reproduced the strict ordering around \(D_c\) whenever the left branch exists and the convergence of both endpoints toward \(D_c\). The exact identities comparing the inverse-hyperbolic arguments with \(z+a\) establish the all-parameter straddling; the finite evaluations are only supplementary.

originality.rationale: The direct 2008/2010 Gürkan--Pashaev paper implication-covers the final claim. It prints the undercritical and overcritical finite-temperature concurrence branches, defines the same critical coupling \(D_c\), and explicitly states that at positive temperature entanglement vanishes on an interval containing \(D_c\) that grows with temperature. The audited \(D_-\) and \(D_+\) formulas are obtained by setting the two printed monotone numerators to zero and applying \(\operatorname{arcosh}\) and \(\operatorname{arsinh}\). The straddling of \(D_c\) follows from elementary hyperbolic identities. Under the required implication standard, lack of printed endpoint notation does not make this original.
